_comment: The Giulia data set's pipeline configuration, v4 (2026-10-15; v4: the search's wall budget 400 h, D-090; the file lives in the project folder hpc/pipeline/projects/giulia/, D-091; v3: the finalist fitted as an ensemble of 10, D-089). One file per data set; every key is required; a key starting with '_' documents the key after it and is ignored. v1 (2026-10-14, log D-085): the direction set by the user -- an expressive NPE network, a large GP search (initial design and guided search) and a large training budget -- with Claude's values; amended 2026-10-15 by D-086 (head_pool_ops searched). v2: the values the user set on 2026-10-15 (D-088) -- the split 85/10/5, 48 cores per trial, one best-fit seed for now, 50 initial points, 20 GP rounds of 10, 20 epochs per trial; every other value is still Claude's, for the user to inspect before any submission. Keys marked NEEDS-CODE are honoured only once the named block of claude/PLAN_2026-10-13_giulia_pipeline.md is built; the driver refuses a config it cannot honour.
_paths: Where everything lives on davinci (absolute; no '~').
_envs: Conda environments: extraction and banks in sbi_export, training and search in sbi_env.
_real: S1, the real-arm extraction (G1). Done for Giulia (cohort manifest 21b7ef03bb7f776b): the driver skips it.
_sim: S2, the simulated-arm re-detection (G2). Done for Giulia (record 7af3759a0f3c1350): skipped.
_freeze: S3, the label freeze (G3). Done for Giulia (29e38c89b08a2dd8): skipped.

exclude.p0_conn: Weibull kernel axis; never drawn under conn_rule=flat, recorded as NaN
exclude.d0_conn: Weibull kernel axis; never drawn under conn_rule=flat, recorded as NaN
exclude.beta_conn: Weibull kernel axis; never drawn under conn_rule=flat, recorded as NaN

_bank: S4-S6, the bank plan and the two banks (B5): the values of export_windows/profiles/giulia.json. Plan of record c8303506131a4632; the banks are being built by the chain line BC: done stages are skipped.
_split: The grouped split by donor (D-076: a donor is one network), train / selection / report = 85 / 10 / 5 % of the donors (the user, D-088): 2,220 / 261 / 131 of the 2,612 donors, about 536,000 / 63,000 / 32,000 rows if donors were equal in size (v1 used the code's fixed 70 / 15 / 15: 1,828 / 392 / 392). The training split is what the network fits, the selection split picks the best epoch (and drives the patience), the report split gives the NLL the GP minimises. NEEDS-CODE (blocks 6-7): the runner's grouped_split fractions are fixed today (run_joint_arms.py:118, no flag, F-i); the runner takes them from a flag and the tuner passes them to every trial, so the split hash and the trial ids change. The same fractions serve the best fit.
_search: S7, the GP search over the joint stack's hyper-parameters. Total trials N = n_initial_points + gp_rounds * trials_per_round = 50 + 20 * 10 = 250.

search._campaign: S-A1: NPE term only, arm A1 (D-039: encoder and flow fitted on simulated windows only). S-A2/S-A5 would put the recordings into the loss; S-A25 cannot run.
search._shape_anchors: Not tuning knobs: p and d_theta are the bank's theta width (23). embedding_dim anchors the flow-width rule, hidden_features in [min(max(32, 2s), 64), max(8s, 256)] for s = max(p, embedding_dim) >= 16: 64 gives [64, 512] (the code's own rule, no change). Passed to EVERY tuner call (F-ar).
search._space_overrides: NEEDS-CODE (block 7: the tuner reads ranges from the config). depth_exponent [3, 6] -> [3, 5]: F-s, the DSN's own configured range; a depth-6 encoder (64 blocks) has 49-215 M parameters against 7-20 M at depth 5 (widths 1.5-3.0, both block families, E 64), and the depth-6 ResNeXt corner costs about 5x the depth-5 ResNeXt corner's time per training row and 3.5x its step memory. embedding_size [8, 16] -> [16, 64]: a summary of at most 16 numbers for 23 parameters can bottleneck the posterior (reasoning; a learned summary tends to a sufficient one only if its dimension is not too small -- Chen et al. 2021 for InfoMax embeddings, as cited by the KB's misspecification-robust SBI paper); the GP chooses within [16, 64]. head_pool_ops [0, 1] (D-086, the user's call of 2026-10-15): a 13th searched axis, NEEDS-CODE in blocks 6-7 (a runner flag --head-pool-ops; the axis in the joint space, today a fixed value no flag carries, F-b): code 0 pools the mean over time of each stage, code 1 the mean, max and std (the DSN's HEAD_POOL_OPS_LEVELS); at the costliest configuration code 1 triples the head's input (640 -> 1920 features) for +0.4 % parameters and +0.6 % time per training row. Every other axis keeps the code's range.
search._flow: NEEDS-CODE (blocks 6-7). conditioner_hidden_layers 2: each spline transform's conditioner is a 2-hidden-layer network whatever num_transforms is (F-ac: from an int, sbi 0.27 gives each conditioner num_transforms hidden layers, 12 at 12 transforms). num_bins 10: the space's declared value, which today never reaches the runner (it builds 8; F-a).
search._n_initial_points: Random configurations before the GP is used, run together as round 0 (they do not depend on each other). 50 (the user, D-088): a fifth of N, about 3.8 per free axis (13 axes with head_pool_ops, D-086).
search._gp_rounds: GP-guided rounds after round 0; each proposes trials_per_round configurations by expected improvement, made distinct by the constant liar. 20 rounds of 10 (the user, D-088): the GP is refitted on every finished trial before each round, 20 times.
search._max_concurrent_trials: At most this many trial jobs at once. 25 (Claude's, following D-088): round 0's 50 run in two waves of 25 (24 would need a third wave for two trials); a GP round runs its 10 at once. 25 x 48 cores = 1,200 cores in round 0, 480 in a GP round.
search._seeds: NEEDS-CODE (block 7: a separate proposal seed). gp_seed drives the proposals (round r uses gp_seed + r); train_seed is every trial's training seed, hence one donor split for the whole search, so trials differ by their configuration alone.
search._gp_noise_sigma: The GP's assumed noise sd in nats; null = estimated from the data (the code's default).
search._trial: One trial = one configuration trained once. NEEDS-CODE (block 6): the budget is in passes over the training split, so every configuration sees the same data whatever its batch size; steps per epoch = ceil(passes / epochs * n_train / batch_size). 6 passes in 20 epochs (epochs: the user, D-088; passes: v1's): each epoch is 0.3 of a pass and ends with the NPE loss over the whole selection split; the best epoch is kept; no early stop (the runner's patience, 99, cannot fire in 20 epochs). resources: a whole 48-core node (ncpus: the user, D-088; dvnode031 has 754 GiB; the costliest configuration needs about 120 GB of step memory at batch 1024). walltime: about 20-49 h projected for the costliest configuration (ResNet blocks, depth 5, width 3, fusion; 22-53 h with 12-layer conditioners), 5-13 h at depth 4, 0.6-1.5 h for the smallest measured [estimate: per-row costs measured on one sandbox core; an assumed 10-24x speed-up on 48 cores; the budget gate measures it on davinci].
search._budget_gate: NEEDS-CODE (block 7). Before round 0: the space's costliest configuration (ResNet blocks, depth 5, width 3.0, fusion, head_pool_ops 1, embedding 64, hidden 512, 12 transforms) trained for probe_steps steps at each searched batch size, plus probe_val_rows validation rows, on the trial resources; the driver STOPs unless the projected trial time x safety_factor fits the trial walltime and the measured memory fits mem. The numbers are written to the state file.
search._max_total_walltime_h: 400 h (the user, D-090: 'put it at 400h and see afterwards if resume'; v3 had 600). Elapsed time since the search started, queue waits included. At the limit no new round starts and running trials finish; the search can be extended later from the ledger under a raised cap. Expected without queue waits: 22 waves (round 0's 50 trials in two, then one per GP round), each as long as its slowest trial -- at most about 18-44 days if every wave held a trial of the costliest size, less when the trials are smaller; the 400 h cap ends the search before round 20 if the mean wave, queue waits included, exceeds about 18 h [estimate, as for the trial walltime].
search._resubmit_killed: A trial killed at its walltime is resubmitted with --resume (block 6), at most max_resubmits times; then it is recorded as killed.

_best_fit: S8, the finalist (the search's lowest report-split NLL) fitted as an ensemble of M_ens = 10 members (the user, D-089), combined as the uniform mixture q_bar(theta | x) = (1/10) sum_m q_omega_m(theta | h_psi_m(x)). Members are independent (encoder, flow) pairs trained with the long budget, one job each. split_seed: the one donor split all members share (D-088 'one seed', read by Claude as one split; to confirm) -- seed 1, a fresh split, since seed 0 is the search's, on which the winner was chosen, so its report NLL there is biased low; member_seeds: the members' training seeds (initialisation, batch order). With one shared split the ensemble's report NLL follows from the members' per-row NLL files (run_joint_arms.py:628-633) by a log-sum-exp, with no rerun. About 5-13 days per member for a costliest-size winner without an early stop, ten nodes at once, 61-145 k core-hours in all [estimate, as for the trial walltime]; past the 300 h walltime a member resumes (block 6). NEEDS-CODE: block 6 (passes, patience_epochs, a split seed apart from the training seed), block 7 (the members, the ensemble NLL).

best_fit._patience_epochs: Stop when the selection-split NLL has not improved for this many epochs (the runner's patience is fixed at 99 today, F-d). An epoch improves only if it beats the best by more than 1e-6 nats per row, the code's margin, kept as it is (D-087).
best_fit._n_posterior_draws: Posterior draws per report row for the final models' diagnostics; not used by the fit in arm A1.

_loader: D-084: the runner streams the bank through a buffer of this many shards (10,000 rows each, about 0.7 GB of windows per shard).
